s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions
salient_findings: Bilateral, symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas on panoramic radiography
Expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of cortical plates on computed tomography
key_facts: Two-year-old boy
Progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
Normal vital signs
No lymphadenopathy
Unremarkable routine hematologic tests
Panoramic radiography showed well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas
Computed tomography showed bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions
Thinning of cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
Mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
No cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions in a young child

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multilocular radiolucent lesions in the jaws

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of jaw swelling and radiolucent lesions, although less common in children

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause jaw swelling and radiolucent lesions, although often associated with other skeletal findings

shortlist.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, but possible cause of jaw swelling and radiolucent lesions in children

raw.rationale: The symmetrical, bilateral, and painless swelling of the jaws, along with the presence of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas on panoramic radiography and expansile lesions on computed tomography, are characteristic of Cherubism, particularly in a two-year-old boy.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with unilateral involvement and more aggressive features

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: Usually associated with abnormal serum biochemistry and other systemic manifestations

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Often presents with ground-glass appearance on radiographs and is less likely to cause symmetrical jaw enlargement

rejected.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a unilateral, rapidly growing lesion with more pronounced cortical expansion and possible cortical breach
